offer: Since the thaw, {creatures} have been bold around {place}. I lost two hens and nearly my nerve. Cull {n} of them, would you?
My cousin won't walk past {place} any more. {creatures}, she says, and more every week. Put down {n} and I'll see you paid.
Something's stirred the {creatures} near {place}. Clear out {n} before they find the road.
kinds.note: {place}, {where}. Anything that isn't a demon counts.
thanks: You smell of blood and bracken, which means you did it. Thank you.
Hah! I'll sleep tonight. Here, take this.
Good. The path to {place} is ours again.

offer: I'm short on {item}, and the season won't wait. Bring me {n} and I'll pay fair.
Could you find me {n} {item}? My hands aren't what they were for the gathering.
{n} {item}. That's all I need to get through the week. Will you?
kinds.note: {giver} is in {town}. Talk to them with the {item} in your pack.
thanks: That'll do nicely. Here's your due.
Just what I needed, and fresher than the market's.

offer: Would you take this to {otherNpc} in {other}? It's nothing much, but it matters to me. Mind the weather on the road.
{otherNpc} in {other} is waiting on this. The carters won't go that way any more. You will, won't you?
A small parcel for {otherNpc}, over in {other}. They'll know what it means.
thanks: Ah, from {giver}! Thank you, traveller. Take this for your trouble.
I'd given up on this. Here, you've earned it.
Safe on the road, I hope? Here's something for the boots.

offer: Folk say lights move at {place} after dark. I'd know if it's true before I send the children berrying. Go and look, then tell me.
Nobody's been out to {place} since my father's day. Is it still standing? I'd pay to know.
I dreamt of {place} three nights running. Humour an old fool: go there and come back.
thanks: Still standing, is it? Well. That settles an argument. Here.
Lights, you say? Hm. Best leave it be. Thank you for looking.
You've a walker's legs. Take this.

offer: {villager} went out toward {place} two days ago and hasn't come back. Please. Find them and bring them home.
Have you seen {villager}? They went looking for mushrooms near {place}. They always come back by supper.
{villager} took a wrong turn chasing a goat, the fool, somewhere near {place}. Bring them back to {town}?
thanks: {villager}! Oh, you're safe. Traveller, I can't thank you enough.
Home in one piece. That's worth more than coin, but have the coin anyway.
You brought them back. The whole town will hear of this.
kinds.escortNote: {villager} follows you. Keep them close: they won't go far alone.
kinds.found: Oh! You came for me? Lead on, I'll stay close.

stories.title: The Lodestone's Hum
stories.offer: You feel it too, don't you? The hum under the floorboards, under the hills. My grandmother called it the Lodestone singing. She said the shrines remember what it sings about. Find out for me?

steps.note: {place}, {where}. Old shrines are where it is loudest.
The tablet stands among the stones of {place}.
Climb any of the great towers and lay your hand on the crystal. The hum is a song the crystals answer.

steps.say: Lodestone iron? Aye. It turns in the hand toward the towers. Ancient stuff. The ruins are full of it, and full of things that guard it.

steps.note: {place}, {where}. Six of whatever keeps watch there.

steps.say: The crystals answer the hum... and the ruins guard its iron. Then the towers are not watchtowers at all. They're tuning forks. Thank you, friend. Drink's on the house, forever.

stories.title: Embers of the Old Watch
stories.offer: Before the dark came every night, there was the Watch: a fire on every hilltop, one town to the next. The last of their banners hangs in a bandit camp now, if you believe the drunks. I believe the drunks.

steps.text: Climb to the old watchtower at {place}
steps.note: {place}, {where}. The Watch lit its fires there.
{other}, {where}. The Watch had a hall there once.
steps.say: The Watch banner. I never thought I'd see it. We'll hang it where the lantern-fire can see it. Go well, Watcher.

stories.title: The Bell Beneath
stories.offer: When the wind is from the old stones, I hear a bell. Down under the ground, like. My dad said there's vaults under the ruins, sealed with riddles. Open one and tell me if there's a bell. Please. I can't sleep for it.

steps.note: {place}, {where}. Look for the vault door among the stones.

steps.text: Open the vault at {place} and defeat its keeper
steps.note: Solve the seal, then face what waits inside.

steps.say: No bell? Just a keeper, and a chest. Hm. Then what have I been hearing? ...Never mind. You've done more than enough.

kinds.name: Starfall
kinds.announce: A star has fallen {where}! Something guards the shard.
kinds.success: The starfall shard is yours to take.
kinds.fail: The shard's glow fades and it crumbles to ash.

kinds.name: Caravan Ambush
kinds.announce: Bandits are attacking a merchant caravan {where}! Defend it.
kinds.success: The caravan rolls on. The merchants won't forget this.
kinds.fail: The caravan is lost. The bandits scatter with the goods.

kinds.name: The Wandering Behemoth
kinds.announce: The Thornhide Behemoth is on the move {where}. Bring friends.
kinds.success: The Behemoth falls with a sound like a felled oak.
kinds.fail: The Behemoth wanders off into the hills.

kinds.name: The Wild Hunt
kinds.announce: Horns in the dark {where}... The Wild Hunt rides tonight.
kinds.success: The Huntsman's horn is silent. The hunt is broken.
kinds.fail: The horns fade toward the hills. The hunt passes on.

kinds.name: The Glintfox
kinds.announce: A Glintfox has been spotted {where}, its tail full of stolen gems! Catch it before it vanishes.
kinds.fail: The Glintfox slips away into the brush.

dungeons.door: A vault door of grey stone, sealed with a glowing sigil.

puzzles.name: The Three Levers
puzzles.hint: Three levers, marked with the sun, the moon and the star. The inscription reads: "{order}, and the way is open."
puzzles.wrong: The levers clatter back. That was not the order.

puzzles.name: The Weighing Stones
puzzles.hint: Three pressure stones. The inscription reads: "All must bear weight at once." They stay down for {hold} seconds.

puzzles.name: The Cold Braziers
puzzles.hint: Two cold braziers flank the door. The inscription reads: "Give the watchers fire."

puzzles.name: The Weeping Font
puzzles.hint: Water wells from a cracked font and runs over the sigil. The inscription reads: "Still the weeping, and I will listen."

tablets.title: The First Hum
tablets.text: Before the towns, before the roads, there was only the Lodestone, sleeping in the deep rock. It dreamt, and its dreaming was a hum, and where the hum was loudest, the first people built their fires.

tablets.title: The Tower Builders
tablets.text: They did not build the towers to watch for enemies. They built them to listen. Each crystal is a shard of the Lodestone's voice, set high so the wind could carry it from valley to valley.

tablets.title: The Breaking
tablets.text: When the Lodestone woke, it did not wake gently. The ground split, the shards scattered, and the night grew teeth. We call the teeth demons. The old ones called them the Unsung: things born where the hum went quiet.

tablets.title: The Sunsteel Oath
tablets.text: Iron drinks the dark. Silver turns it aside. But sunsteel, ore that has slept a hundred years in a shaft of daylight, remembers the sun, and the Unsung cannot bear to be remembered at.

tablets.title: Of the Watch
tablets.text: There were a thousand fires on a thousand hills, and every fire could see two more. While the Watch burned, no town was ever alone in the dark. The last fire went out in a winter no one wrote down.

tablets.title: The Vault Wardens
tablets.text: We sealed the deep vaults with riddles, not locks. A lock can be broken by any brute. A riddle opens only for one who stops and thinks, and the Unsung never stop.

tablets.title: On Wardbloom
tablets.text: Plant it in a ring and the dark walks around. Nobody knows why. The gardeners say the flowers hum, too quietly for us, loudly enough for the night.

tablets.title: The Glintfox
tablets.text: A fox with a tail like a jeweller's purse. It steals whatever glitters and runs from whoever looks. Children are told that if you catch one, it will drop everything it ever took. Children are told many things.

tablets.title: The Wild Hunt
tablets.text: On the darkest nights, the Huntsman rides with his hollow hounds. He does not hunt deer. He hunts the brave, because the brave are the only ones out after dark.

tablets.title: The Thornhide
tablets.text: It is older than the towns. It eats nothing and sleeps nowhere. It walks from one end of the world to the other and back, and where it has walked the briars grow thick for a year.

tablets.title: Falling Stars
tablets.text: When a star falls, the sky gives back a shard of what the Breaking scattered. Starmetal, the smiths call it. The guardians that rise with it are only the sky's way of asking whether you deserve it.

tablets.title: The Road Charter
tablets.text: Let it be written: any merchant who travels between two lit towns travels under the protection of both. Let it also be written: the bandits never signed this.

tablets.title: The Shrine Keepers
tablets.text: The keepers tended the shrines until the last of them grew old. They left their tablets for whoever came after, so that the hum would never be entirely forgotten.

tablets.title: Voidglass
tablets.text: Deep under the oldest hills the rock turns black and cold and clear. Look into it and you see nothing at all. That is the most frightening thing about it.

tablets.title: A Note on Slimes
tablets.text: Dewdrop slimes are harmless, mostly. They are the morning dew that the Lodestone's hum has taught to wander. Be kind to them. Or don't. They will not remember either way.

tablets.title: The Last Keeper
tablets.text: I am the last who remembers the song. I have written it on every stone I could reach. If you are reading this, then the stones did their work, and so must you. Listen.

codex.lore: Thornback boars charge first and think never. The bristles on their spine are stiff enough to stop an arrow.
Moss grows in the fur of the old ones. They hunt in pairs and remember the faces of those who escape them.
A crag ram will charge a cliff to prove it is the stronger. It usually is.
Its breath freezes in the air and falls as needles. The rime stalker follows tracks in the snow for days.
Armoured, patient and venomous. Dust scuttlers wait under the sand for a footstep.
The bog lurker looks like a mossy log until it does not. It spits mud to blind its prey.
Most cutthroats were farmers once. The nights took their farms; the roads took the rest of them.
Bandit archers keep their distance and their arrows cheap. Close the gap and they panic.
Big, slow and proud of it. A bandit brute stamps the ground before it strikes; listen for it.
Stone guardians set by the vault wardens. They still keep their old posts, long after anyone remembers the orders.
A flicker of the hum given a mind. Wisps guard the places the Lodestone's song once filled.
Ember imps are born where a wildfire burned hottest. They giggle. Nobody likes the giggling.
A snowflake that refused to melt, then refused to stop growing.
Where lightning strikes twice, a spark wisp is left behind to make it three times.
Riverbank clay that the hum woke up. It is slow, heavy, and very sure of itself.
Gale harpies ride the updrafts above cliffs and dive on anything that looks soft.
Drawn to lanterns, campfires and wanderers carrying either. Its wings leave glowing dust on your sleeves.
A shadow that forgot what cast it. Shades are drawn to warmth, which they cannot hold.
Small, fast and wrong. Void mites chew holes in the air itself.
Pale, many-legged and blind. Cave crawlers find you by the sound of your heartbeat.
They hang in their thousands in the deep chambers and wake all at once.
Grown, not made, from the crystal veins of the deep. Its fists ring like bells.
Morning dew that learned to wander. Mostly harmless. Mostly.
An older, greener slime. Moss grows in it, and small snails live on the moss.
The lesser Unsung. They come at dusk in packs and flee from sunsteel and Light.
A greater Unsung wreathed in cinders. Ordinary steel only makes it angry.
It hurls lances of black ice from afar. Only Light or sunsteel will end it.
A greater Unsung that rides the lightning. It rushes faster than you can run.
It slams the ground hard enough to open old graves. Some say that is the point.
Its claws tear the wind itself. Stay out of its wide arc.
It leaps from shadow to shadow and lands where you were standing.

codex.habitat: Light and void regions, at night
codex.lore: A mouth that opens onto nothing. It gnashes in a wide circle around itself.
A lord of the Unsung that walks only when the moon is dark. Its meteors fall on everyone who dares to stand against it.

codex.habitat: Great ruins, sunken temples, demon lairs
codex.lore: The vault wardens' greatest work. A Warden still guards the heart of every great ruin.
The tower-wizards left behind more than books. An Archon still studies in each tower, and resents interruptions.
The last guardian of a sealed vault. When it raises its staff, a sigil burns on the ground: do not be standing in it.
A thief with a tail full of stolen gems. It never fights, only runs. Catch it and it drops its hoard.
Hollow hounds of the Wild Hunt. Unlike the Unsung, they bleed like any beast.
The Huntsman. Antlered, silent, and patient. He hurls his spear at whoever runs.
It rises from the crater with the shard, built of starmetal and old light, and tests anyone who comes for the prize.
Older than the towns. Briars grow wherever it has walked. It shakes the earth when it is angry, and it is easily angered.

species.name: Silverfin Minnow
species.lore: Every child's first fish. They school in the shallows and flash like dropped coins.

species.name: Reed Perch
species.lore: Striped green and gold to hide in the reeds. Bold, hungry and not very clever.

species.name: Speckled Trout
species.lore: It holds in the current behind a stone and takes whatever the river brings it.

species.name: Mudback Carp
species.lore: Old, heavy and patient. A mudback carp can live longer than the angler who hooks it.

species.name: Tidewing Mackerel
species.lore: Its fins are long enough to glide a little above the waves when it is chased.

species.name: Sandflat Flounder
species.lore: Both its eyes are on one side. It does not seem bothered by this.

species.name: Bog Pike
species.habitat: Wetland and forest waters at dusk
species.lore: A mouth full of needles and a temper to match. It strikes at anything that moves in the evening light.

species.name: Frostgill Char
species.lore: Its gills are rimmed with frost even in summer. The highland folk say it keeps the water cold.

species.name: Emberscale Loach
species.habitat: Warm badland waters under a clear sky
species.lore: Its scales are warm to the touch. Cooks swear it seasons itself.

species.name: Gloam Eel
species.lore: It rises when the Unsung walk and glows faintly when it is afraid. It is usually afraid.

species.name: Stormray
species.lore: It comes to the surface when lightning is near and drinks the rain. Its sting tingles for days.

species.name: Moonlit Koi
species.habitat: Still lowland lakes on clear nights
species.lore: White and silver like the moon on the water. They say each one remembers a wish.

species.name: Humming Sturgeon
species.lore: Older than the towers. It hums the Lodestone's note under the water, and the rod hums with it.

species.name: Deepmaw
species.habitat: The open sea on a stormy night
species.lore: Sailors' stories call it a reef until it opens its mouth. Nobody believes the ones who say they landed it.
